claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my daughter Alex. She's 8 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one daughter, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. We both live together here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. 

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for her needs such as food, clothes, and other day-to-day expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually a bit complicated at the moment. Alex has been in hospital for a while now - a few months actually. So I'm not sure if that affects things?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I understand this must be a difficult time for you. The length of the hospital stay can affect Child Benefit, so I need to understand the situation better.

**How long has Alex been in hospital? Can you tell me approximately how many weeks she has been there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 15 weeks now. She's been in the hospital ward all that time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I understand Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks.

This is an important detail because after 12 weeks in hospital, Child Benefit can be affected. However, there are exceptions to this rule.

**Do you regularly spend money on Alex while she's in hospital? For example, do you buy her things like clothes, toys, books, or other items for her?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: To be honest, I'm not really sure. I mean, I visit her when I can, but with everything going on... I haven't really been keeping track of whether I've been spending money on things for her or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it's a very stressful situation and it's completely understandable that you haven't been keeping track of everything.

Let me ask this another way to help clarify: **Since Alex has been in hospital, have you purchased anything for her at all? For example, things like new pyjamas, slippers, books, games, toiletries, treats, or anything else - even small items?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really can't say for certain. Like I said, with everything that's been happening, I honestly don't know if I've been spending money on her needs while she's been in there. It's all been such a blur.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - you're dealing with a very challenging situation.

Let me ask you one more question to complete the assessment: **Before Alex went into hospital, were you living with her and responsible for her care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Before she went into hospital, she lived at home with me and I took care of her completely - I still do, she just happens to be in the hospital right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I have enough details now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain the situation:

**General Eligibility:** You meet the basic criteria for Child Benefit because:
- Alex is under 16 (she's 8 years old)
- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- You were responsible for her care before she went into hospital
- You still consider yourself responsible for her

**However, there is a complication:** Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week limit. According to the rules, after a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, your entitlement to Child Benefit is usually affected.

**There is an exception:** You can continue to receive Child Benefit after 12 weeks if you regularly spend money on your child while they're in hospital. Unfortunately, you've indicated that you're uncertain whether you've been spending money on Alex's needs during her hospital stay.

Because of this uncertainty about whether you meet the exception criteria, I cannot definitively determine your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**My recommendation:** I strongly encourage you to contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific situation. They can:
- Review your exact circumstances in detail
- Help you work out if any purchases you may have made count as "regularly spending money" on Alex
- Advise you on your continued entitlement

You should also inform them about Alex's hospital stay if you haven't already done so, as this is an important change in circumstances that needs to be reported.

I hope Alex recovers soon and is able to come home.
